title: The Bitter Layout or: How I Learned to Love the Model Picker — Maximillian Piras, Yutori
talk_summary: A design talk arguing that AI app UIs converge on a 'bitter layout' (chat input + model picker) because models are not commoditized, so interfaces must conform to the next model rather than optimize usability. It is mostly UX/design theory with no engineering mechanisms, benchmarks, or agent-system practices.

takeaways.technique: Treat model choice as a mode selector, not a user-facing dropdown
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues the model picker is effectively a mode selector (like caps lock) that changes output drastically, and that users shouldn't have to match models to modes manually.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think that the model picker is a bit of a mode selector as well

takeaways.technique: Design for absorbing the next model cheaply
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues the winning property of a layout is that a new model can be dropped in with one line change, making the app instantly more capable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just add one line item and now your app is NX more intelligent
